description: A team of space enthusiasts, curious minds, and problem-solvers working together to turn ideas into impact. 🚀
summary:
The Unforgotten: A Message Across the Stars, is a storytelling project that brings some of NASA's historic space explorers to life through the perspective of a curious alien astronaut. Throughout the story, the alien astronaut encounters Pioneer 10, Galileo, Sojourner, the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle and the Kepler Space Telescope, learning about their missions, discoveries and contributions to humanity's understanding of space.

The project addresses the challenge by highlighting the achievements of space exploration equipment whose missions have ended or which are no longer operational. Through conversations between the alien astronaut and these explorers, we show that even when a mission comes to an end, the knowledge and discoveries it leaves behind continue to matter.

More than just sharing scientific facts, our project is about gratitude, curiosity and legacy. It reminds us that these machines may have travelled far from Earth, but they have never truly been forgotten. We hope the story inspires the next generation to look up at the night sky, ask questions and continue exploring the unknown.
details:
How Does Our Project Work, and What Impact Do We Hope to Make?

Our project is a short animated storytelling experience that brings historic NASA space exploration missions to life. It follows an alien astronaut travelling through space and encountering five remarkable explorers: Pioneer 10, Galileo, Sojourner, the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle and the Kepler Space Telescope. Through conversations with each of them, the alien learns about their missions, the discoveries they made and the important role they played in expanding humanity's understanding of the universe.

Rather than simply presenting facts about these missions, we chose to tell their stories in a more personal and engaging way. Each explorer gets the opportunity to share its own achievements, almost as if it is looking back on its journey. The story eventually shifts to two teenagers looking at the night sky, connecting the achievements of past missions with the curiosity and potential of the next generation.

Tools and software used

We used a combination of creative software and AI-assisted tools to develop our project:

  • Clipchamp: Used for video editing, arranging scenes and bringing the final storytelling experience together.
  • ibisPaint X: Used for creating and editing illustrations and visual elements.
  • Blender: Used for developing 3D visuals and enhancing the visual representation of space and its explorers.
  • Canva: Used for designing and preparing visual assets and other presentation elements.
  • ChatGPT and Claude: Used as AI-assisted tools to refine the script, improve dialogue, develop the narrative flow and make the storytelling more engaging. The creative direction, original script and final decisions remained ours.

Benefits and intended impact

One of the main benefits of our project is that it makes space exploration history more approachable, especially for younger audiences. Scientific missions can sometimes seem distant or complicated, and their achievements are often reduced to technical facts and figures. By giving these explorers a voice and a personality, we hope to create a stronger emotional connection between the audience and the missions.

Our intended impact goes beyond teaching people about individual spacecraft. We want viewers to recognize that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its significance. The data collected, discoveries made and questions raised by these explorers continue to contribute to science and inspire future research. We also hope to encourage young people to develop an interest in astronomy, space science and exploration.

What makes our project creative?

Our main creative decision was to tell the story from the perspective of an alien astronaut. Instead of having a narrator simply explain what each spacecraft accomplished, we imagined an outsider discovering humanity's achievements and helping us see them from a different perspective. This allowed us to combine scientific information with imagination, emotion and storytelling.

We also wanted to create a meaningful connection between the past and the future of space exploration. The final scene, featuring two teenagers wondering about the mysteries of the night sky, represents the next generation of explorers who may one day continue the work started by these missions.

Factors we considered

While developing the project, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: We aimed to represent each mission's actual purpose, achievements and historical significance accurately.
  • Audience engagement: We wanted the story to be understandable and interesting, particularly for school-age audiences.
  • Emotional connection: We wanted viewers to appreciate these missions not just as machines, but as important parts of humanity's journey into space.
  • Creativity and originality: We explored an imaginative narrative that could communicate scientific achievements in a fresh and memorable way.
  • Educational value: We made sure that the storytelling remained informative and that the audience could learn something meaningful about every explorer featured.
  • Visual presentation: We considered how animation, illustrations, 3D visuals and editing could work together to make the experience more immersive.

Ultimately, we wanted to create something that would leave the audience with one simple thought: a mission may end, but the discoveries it leaves behind never do.
